song.title: Dans la salle du Bar-tabac de la rue Des Martyrs

guitar.evidence: No reliable specific knowledge of this French band's gear.

tone.target: bright edge-of-breakup rhythm with wah color
tone.profile: bright edge-of-breakup rhythm with wah color
tone.summary: The signal chain uses a light boost for definition, followed by the V-Wah for color, feeding into a Fender/Vox style amp (AC30 TB) paired with a bright 4x12 cabinet. A subtle Room reverb adds space without muddying the rhythm.

rig.name: Pigalle - Dans la salle du Bar-tabac de la rue Des Martyrs - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Slightly boost the signal for definition and cut through the mix.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate a clean, subtle tone shaping rather than a dedicated OD pedal, matching the 'bistro rhythm' feel.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required 'wah color' and rhythmic articulation.
Achieve the 'clean-to-light crunch' without heavy fuzz or high gain.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen for its classic, non-aggressive breakup sound, simulating a Vox/Fender style clean overdrive.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the required Vox/Fender-style small combo amp tone (AC30).
Provide a bright and articulate platform for the rhythm tone.
blocks.gap: While the AC30 suggests British voicing, the UK Vintage 4x12 provides the necessary brightness and punch for this specific 'bistro' sound.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the upper mids and brightness as requested, while slightly taming the low end.
Add a subtle 'short room' ambience without sounding lush or muddy.

improvements.summary: Refine cabinet and IR to better match the small combo/bistro aesthetic while maintaining brightness.

proposals.reason: A smaller, more vintage cabinet (e.g., 2x12) better suits the small combo/bistro vibe than a large 4x12.
